title.rendered: All Authority in Heaven and on Earth: The Gospel For Today

excerpt.rendered: All authority in heaven and on earth has been given to Me. Then Jesus turns and sends His followers into the world. The commission is not from a delegated ruler. It is from the highest throne in the universe.

content.rendered:
All authority in heaven and on earth has been given to Me. Then Jesus turns and sends His followers into the world. The commission is not from a delegated ruler. It is from the highest throne in the universe. Everything the believer walks in flows from this one sentence.

The Gospel For Today | Tuesday, July 14, 2026

Today’s Scripture

“Then Jesus came to them and said, ‘All authority in heaven and on earth has been given to me. Therefore go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, and teaching them to obey everything I have commanded you. And surely I am with you always, to the very end of the age.'”
Matthew 28:18-20 (NIV)

Today’s Message

Matthew 28 records the last words Jesus spoke on earth before ascending to the Father. Every syllable matters. Jesus opens with a declaration of universal authority. All authority in heaven and on earth has been given to Me. Not some authority. Not most. All. The Greek word is pasa. It leaves nothing outside the sphere of Christ’s rule.

This declaration is the foundation of everything that follows in the Great Commission. Because Jesus has all authority, He can send His followers to any nation on earth with a message that overrides every competing authority in that nation’s culture, government, religious system, or spiritual realm. Because Jesus has all authority, the disciples can baptise in a name that stands over every other name. Because Jesus has all authority, they can teach commands that carry the weight of the throne of God itself. And because Jesus has all authority, His promise to be with them always is not sentiment. It is the guarantee of the King who cannot be evicted from any territory the believer walks into.

Yesterday we saw that the believer has been given exousia. Today we see where that exousia comes from. It is not intrinsic to us. It is delegated. It flows down from the throne where Jesus is now seated. The believer standing in spiritual authority is not standing on their own resources. They are standing on borrowed weight. The weight belongs to the King who has all authority in heaven and on earth. He shares it with those who have been placed in Him.

This is a critically important distinction for Gospelbuzz readers who have grown up in traditions that either overplay or underplay the believer’s authority. Overplay says the believer somehow acquires personal spiritual power through their own practice or ritual. Underplay says the believer has no meaningful role in spiritual conflict at all. The New Testament sits in neither place. The believer has real, exercised authority in the spiritual realm, because Jesus who has all authority has delegated it to them. And the believer only ever has that authority because Jesus first has it and gives it. The moment we forget where the authority comes from, we forget that we are servants of the King, not kings ourselves.

For Gospelbuzz readers today, the truth is settled. All authority belongs to Jesus. He shares it with those He sends. When you speak in the name of Jesus, you are not speaking in your own name. You are speaking in the name of the One who holds all authority in heaven and on earth. Walk in that today. Speak in that today. And go into your day trusting that the One with all authority is with you always, to the very end of the age.

Prayer

Father, I acknowledge that all authority in heaven and on earth has been given to Jesus. Every authority I walk in flows from His throne. I am not standing on my own resources. I am standing on the delegated authority of the King who has all authority. Because He has sent me, I go. Because He is with me always, I am not alone in any territory I walk into today. His name is over every other name. His authority is above every other authority. I walk in that reality today, confident in the One who has commissioned me. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

All authority in heaven and on earth belongs to Jesus. He has delegated His authority to me as one who is sent. I walk in that authority today. He is with me always.
